Issue #5: Better handling of links to other sites We render our product docs with Python-Markdown and readers keep complaining that when they click a link to another website they lose their place in the docs. Other tools we've tried seem to handle external links better out of the box. Could Python-Markdown do something smarter with external links? I'm not sure what the best approach is, just that the current behaviour isn't great for documentation sites. --- maintainer comment 1 by @AvAdiii --- Thanks for the questions. Decisions: 1. Add a new built-in extension called `external_links`, loaded with `extensions=['external_links']`. Nothing changes unless it is enabled. 2. Every external `` element gets `target="_blank"` and `rel="noopener noreferrer"`. This includes automatic links like ``. 4. Images are not affected. No configuration options for now. input.summary: The processing logic works, but there is no entry point in pyproject.toml. The issue's required usage, `extensions=['external_links']`, therefore raises ModuleNotFoundError. ARCHITECTURE.md also requires an entry point for every built-in extension. The tests only pass because they import the class directly.

findings.title: Missing entry point: extensions=['external_links'] fails
findings.evidence: `python -c "import markdown; markdown.markdown('<https://example.com>', extensions=['external_links'])"` raised `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'external_links'`. pyproject.toml has no `external_links` line under `[project.entry-points.'markdown.extensions']`. ARCHITECTURE.md requires one for every built-in extension, and the issue requires loading by short name.

findings.title: Tests never load the extension by its short name
findings.evidence: Both tests pass `ExternalLinksExtension()` directly, so the missing entry point goes undetected. The tests also do not cover autolinks, images, `mailto:` links, `#anchor` links, or reference-style links. The issue explicitly names autolinks and images.

findings.title: Treeprocessor priority 3 runs after unescape (0 < 3 is earlier, but ordering is arbitrary)
findings.evidence: Registry priorities: inline 20, prettify 10, external_links 3, unescape 0. It works, because inline links are already in the tree by then, but the priority is not justified.

own_checks.check: Autolink, inline, reference and image behaviour (class loaded directly)

The `HTTPS://` uppercase scheme is not treated as external. The issue says 'starts with', so this is acceptable.
